transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Halcyon Head of AI), Liam O'Connor (Halcyon Lead Platform Engineer), Nina Brooks (CTO)

[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - i'm Jordan, AE for Halcyon; priya is our SE, she'll run most of the console walkthrough. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marta Ruiz: Good, thanks. excited to see the cost bit especially, our CFO will want the per-route numbers.
[00:12] Nina Brooks: Hey all, high level - we care about predictable latency for checkout flows and low cost for bulk background tasks.
[00:20] Priya Patel: great. today's agenda: live Console tour, per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns, quick Q&A, then next steps for a pilot. i'll start with the usage analytics landing page.
[00:35] [screen share noise] Priya Patel: so this is the usage analytics page - you can see total token usage, request counts, and a model mix over time. we surface both aggregate and per-route metrics. so if you click into a route like "checkout_autocomplete" you get this per-route dashboard.
[00:50] Liam O'Connor: sorry interrupt, can you filter by environment? we have staging vs prod and want to compare.
[00:54] Priya Patel: yes, top left filter - env, model version, and time range. staging/prod split is common.
[01:05] Priya Patel: in the per-route view you get latency percentiles, token distribution, bun- sorry, token distribution by request, and cost attribution. cost attribution is where we map the token usage to a per-token unit cost plus infra overhead.
[01:20] Jordan Kim: quick note: cost is per-route by default using tagging from your gateway, but we can also do model-level or team-level grouping.
[01:30] Marta Ruiz: when you say "per-token unit cost" is that just model inference, or does it include queuing and overhead?
[01:36] Priya Patel: good question. it's model inference + a few platform overheads. we break down into model compute, batching efficiency (i.e., effective tokens/second), KV cache hit rates, and network egress. we show a stacked bar so you can see each component. sometimes the "overhead" can be 10-15% for small, chatty requests.
[01:58] Priya Patel: here's an example: checkout_autocomplete - you can see 95th p95 latency at 110ms on Dedicated, token per-request avg 80 tokens, and cost per 1k tokens is broken down.
[02:12] [00:02:12] Nina Brooks: 110ms p95 on Dedicated is promising. what about hosted?
[02:18] Priya Patel: hosted will be slightly more variable - p95 often 150-220ms depending on burst. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail latencies at scale because of reserved GPU pools.
[02:30] Liam O'Connor: can you show the CSV export of the per-route cost? we need to import into our finance models.
[02:34] Priya Patel: absolutely, export button here - you can choose time range and grouping. i'll export a 30-day sample during the call and attach.
[02:45] [screen noise, click] Priya Patel: exported. note that the CSV columns include route_tag, model_version, requests, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_compute_cost, batching_efficiency_loss, kv_cache_hit_rate, egress_cost, and total_cost_usd.
[02:58] Marta Ruiz: nice. is batching_efficiency_loss something we can improve from our side or something Redwood controls?
[03:05] Priya Patel: it's both - batching benefits from more parallel requests; so client-side shaping (like slightly delaying non-interactive tasks) helps. Redwood Optimize has suggestions and can recommend batching window sizes per route. we also show where quantization would change model_compute_cost.
[03:20] Jordan Kim: fwiw we've seen customers move background jobs to a cheaper model variant or batch them to cut 40% of cost on some routes.
[03:30] Nina Brooks: what's the friction to run two models for a route? e.g., cheap fallback for non-critical and high-quality for checkout.
[03:36] Priya Patel: in the console you can set route policies - primary/secondary models, canary percent, and automatic fallback. routing respects model architecture compatibility; switching to a smaller model is a config change and we surface expected quality delta estimates if you run the eval set.
[03:55] [05:55?] Liam O'Connor: can you break down the per-token cost math quickly? CFO loves deterministic numbers.
[04:05] Priya Patel: sure - base formula: total_cost = model_compute_cost + infra_overhead + network + amortized storage. model_compute_cost is compute_time * GPU_price_per_second; compute_time depends on seq lengths and attention type. we then divide by tokens processed to get per-token. batching increases tokens/sec and lowers per-token compute_time because kernels amortize.
[04:30] Marta Ruiz: are KV cache hits shown in the per-route dashboard? we heavily reuse context for conversation features.
[04:36] Priya Patel: yes - KV cache hit rate is a metric and we also show how cache hits reduce tokens generated and therefore cost. if you have long prefix reuse we show an estimated token savings line.
[04:50] Jordan Kim: also worth mentioning prefix caching / persistent KV caching is available in Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted has TTL-based caching.
[05:00] Nina Brooks: on security - we need SOC2 Type II, ISO, and logs for auditors. can you point to those controls?
[05:06] Jordan Kim: yes, we'll share the SOC2 docs. Dedicated and Private come with richer audit log retention and optional customer-managed KMS.
[05:15] Priya Patel: and for Private we support VPC peering or on-prem packages; key management via your KMS/HSM is supported. there can be a bit more ops work but it's standard for regulated customers.
[05:30] [05:30] Marta Ruiz: ok, so pilot - we'd like a 1-week benchmark on Dedicated with our top 3 routes: checkout_autocomplete, order_summary, customer_support_summary. can you run a cost baseline and latency SLO targets?
[05:44] Jordan Kim: yes, we typically do a pilot - we provision a small Dedicated pool, run your traffic replay or synthetic load, and deliver per-route dashboards + cost CSV.
[05:52] Priya Patel: for benchmarks we need sample prompts and estimated traffic. Liam, can you share your route config and QPS estimates?
[05:58] Liam O'Connor: yes i'll send a list; quick Q: how do you handle padding for variable-length requests? it's inflating our cost in tests.
[06:05] Priya Patel: padding depends on batching window and kernel execution; we surface an "effective tokens" metric that accounts for padding. we also recommend bucketing requests by length on client side when possible.
[06:18] Jordan Kim: competitor question - Marta asked earlier whether we looked at Anthropic / OpenAI pricing. we do; pricing comparison will be included in the doc we send but remember those vendors don't offer same Dedicated/reserved model with per-route dashboards out of the box.
[06:33] Marta Ruiz: internal self-hosting is on the table, but ops cost is the concern - can you summarize operational savings?
[06:39] Jordan Kim: typically customers save on cluster ops, driver/kernel tuning, and ongoing infra optimization. Redwood handles kernel selection, quantization profiles, and autoscaling policies. ops cost savings vary but we can provide a rough TCO comparison.
[06:52] Priya Patel: back to the console: here's the per-route anomaly detection - it flags sudden cost spikes and quality regressions; we tie that to evals so you can see if a model change caused a quality drift.
[07:05] Nina Brooks: good - we had an incident once where a model update doubled hallucinations for a route. will your console show that?
[07:12] Priya Patel: yes, you can pin a route's eval prompts and set regression thresholds; alerts can go to Slack/email/ops.
[07:20] [07:20] Liam O'Connor: for the pilot, will we be able to test quantized model variants? we want to see cost/quality tradeoffs.
[07:26] Priya Patel: absolutely - we can provision INT8 or other quantized variants; Optimize will recommend the best quantization for your workload and show expected cost delta and an estimated quality score change from our eval harness.
[07:40] Marta Ruiz: what about RBAC and team-level cost visibility? finance wants per-product spend.
[07:46] Jordan Kim: Console supports team/org-level views and RBAC. you can restrict who sees billing vs dev metrics. we also support cost center tags so finance can chargeback per product.
[07:58] Priya Patel: showing the billing breakdown now - you can map routes to cost centers and export a ledger for accounting.
[08:08] [08:08] Nina Brooks: any caveats about egress costs if we use hosted? we have customers in EU and US.
[08:15] Priya Patel: egress depends on region; we show egress as a separate line item per route. for cross-region traffic we recommend deploying in-region or using Dedicated in the region to minimize egress.
[08:28] Jordan Kim: also we can put a cap/alert on unexpected spend so you don't get surprises.
[08:34] Marta Ruiz: let's talk numbers - show me an example cost breakdown for the three routes you suggested.
[08:40] Priya Patel: pulling a sample dashboard: checkout_autocomplete - 150k requests/day, avg 80 tokens/request, model_compute $0.045 per 1k tokens, batching inefficiency $0.007, kv cache saves $0.006, total per 1k tokens $0.046 net. order_summary - heavier, avg 420 tokens/request, model_compute $0.22 per 1k tokens, net $0.23 per 1k tokens. customer_support_summary - 1k tokens on average, cheaper model variant recommended for background summarization at $0.09 per 1k tokens.
[09:15] Liam O'Connor: those model_compute numbers, are those for our target GPUs or generic?
[09:19] Priya Patel: those are sample numbers normalized to our GPU pricing for Dedicated NVX-2 style GPUs - we'll run a targeted benchmark to get you exact numbers.
[09:30] Marta Ruiz: is there a minimum commit for Dedicated? our legal team will check.
[09:34] Jordan Kim: there's a baseline reserved capacity proposal for pilots; enterprise Dedicated has monthly commits, but pilot options exist with limited reserved capacity. i'll include our standard commitment tiers in the pricing doc.
[09:46] [09:46] Nina Brooks: timeline - we want a pilot in two weeks. is that doable?
[09:50] Priya Patel: yes, assuming we get your traffic profile and prompts this week. setup is normally 3-5 business days for a small Dedicated pool.
[09:57] Jordan Kim: i'll coordinate with our onboarding team - next actions: we'll send pricing, SOC2 & ISO docs, sample CSV, and a pilot plan.
[10:06] Marta Ruiz: sounds good. quick followup - will the console surface model rollouts and what percentage of traffic was on older model versions?
[10:13] Priya Patel: yes - rollout history and per-model metrics are in the model catalog and per-route timeline.
[10:20] [10:20] Liam O'Connor: one last technical: can you run a replay of our production traffic to your Dedicated pool for bench? any PII concerns?
[10:28] Priya Patel: we can do traffic replay with either anonymized prompts or run it in Private deployment. for hosted pilot we recommend anonymization or synthetic replay; for exact same data you'd choose Private or Dedicated with your compliance controls.
[10:42] Nina Brooks: ok that answers it.
[10:45] Jordan Kim: recap and next steps - Jordan to send pricing + commitment tiers, Priya to share recording and dashboard export, Liam to share traffic and prompts, Marta to confirm pilot criteria. we'll aim for pilot week of 2026-05-25.
[10:58] Marta Ruiz: thanks everyone, appreciate the walkthrough.
[11:02] Jordan Kim: thanks all, will follow up.

-- End transcript --
notes: Customer leaning toward Dedicated for checkout latency guarantees
Finance care: needs per-route CSV and clear cost math
Security gating: SOC2, KMS, VPC options required for pilot with real data
Pilot scope: 3 routes, 1-week benchmarks, quantization tests
